newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Dominican officials promise crash report next week.
newsitem.headline: Dominican officials promise crash report next week.

text.p: Investigators in the Dominican Republic are close to completing their investigation into the crash early this year of a chartered aircraft that claimed the lives of 189 people.

Vitelio Mejia, director of the Office of Civil Aviation, said he planned a news conference on Nov. 1 to announce the results of the investigation. He said he could not confirm a report by German television station Sat1 that investigators would say the crash was caused by a series of mistakes including human error and mechanical failure.

On Feb. 6, 1996, a chartered Boeing 757 owned by Turkish airline Birgen Air crashed shortly after takeoff on a flight from the Dominican Republic resort of Puerto Plata to Frankfurt and Berlin. The crash into the ocean off the Caribbean nation killed 189 crew and passengers, many of them Germans on holiday.
